cap: Dashboard of Brazil’s 2026 presidential runoff: results by state, voting abroad, polls vs. result and statistical analysis.
Final count: Lula (PT) re-elected with 51.79% of valid votes, 64.3 million votes. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) took 48.21%.
The map shows the winner in each state: red for Lula, blue for Flávio. The stronger the color, the wider the lead. Hover a state for its numbers and flag.
Region buttons highlight a group of states. Lula won all nine Northeast states; Flávio swept the South and the Center-West.
The strip below sums up Brazilians voting abroad: Lula 53.86% vs. Flávio 46.14%.
The lead chart ranks states from Lula’s widest margin (Piauí) to Flávio’s (Roraima). Minas Gerais was the closest race.
The full table can be sorted by any column and filtered with the search box.
Analysis: each dot is a state, placed by Lula’s share. Region explains 79% of the variation in the vote across states (eta²).
How close each state was: only 2 states, Minas Gerais and Tocantins, were decided by less than 5 points.
Uniform swing simulator: moving 1.79 points from Lula to Flávio in every state would have flipped the national result.
Polls vs. result: a sample-weighted regression projected Lula at 49.5%. He got 51.79%, 2.3 points more.
The chance of winning, recalculated each day, had Flávio as the favorite in the final stretch.
Every pollster underestimated Lula. A Brier score of 0.354 is worse than always saying 50% (0.25).
Abroad, Lula won Paris, London, Lisbon and New York; Flávio won Miami, Boston, Tokyo and Nagoya.
